statements.text: President Trump announced a reciprocal energy ceasefire, and President Zelenskyy has assured the Prime Minister that Ukraine would immediately implement it once a start date is confirmed.
The Prime Minister has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military support and fiscal packages to provide urgent support in the coming weeks.

The government has announced new funding to help Ukraine get through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and a new sanctions package that brings over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity under UK sanctions.

The UK is delivering £45 million of surface-to-air missiles to Ukraine and will accelerate deliveries of British Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. The UK has already committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5,000 of them over the next four years, and will accelerate £10 million of the £45 million package for Ukraine's most urgent winter needs.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK's rock-solid support for Ukraine is vital for keeping the UK safe, that the UK is with Ukraine for as long as it takes, and that Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on the continent.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor John Healey will use IMF meetings in Bangkok to urge partners to fully implement an equivalent ban on Russian LNG, and he urged partners to back the ban to curtail the war chest funding Putin.

The Prime Minister welcomed President Zelenskyy to Downing Street, where the leaders underlined that Russia had no interest in peace, and the Prime Minister set out the UK's latest package of Lightweight Multirole Missiles.

The Prime Minister said the UK would continue to develop innovative military solutions for use on the battlefield in Ukraine, including retrofitting British capability onto equipment gifted by other partners, and would continue its diplomatic efforts to support international supplies of defensive equipment.

The UK assesses that the RAF Fairford incident is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard, and the government will bring further sanctions to restrict Iran and the IRGC's capacity to do harm.
Britain has decided to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia for air-to-air refuelling support, and a Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions.

The UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November, with a trade deal on food and drink products, emissions trading progress, a youth experience scheme and deeper immigration cooperation on the table; a food and drink deal is expected to add the equivalent of over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040.

The Prime Minister said the UK's chances at the summit would be enhanced by being open to discussing its relationship with the EU in the longer term, and that after the summit he believes a serious dialogue on the options for that relationship should be set up.
The Prime Minister and Chancellor Merz agreed a new partnership to tackle Russian hybrid threats, and the UK has committed to establish a new National Centre for Information Defence.
The Prime Minister raised the Falkland Islands and the islanders' declared will to remain British with President Trump, and said the UK will always do whatever it takes to uphold their will.
The UK will place AI centre stage in its G20 presidency in 2027 and aims to agree a single set of global principles and standards on AI during that year.

Andy Burnham made an offer to the Scottish Government to work with the UK government on a new model of regional empowerment for Scotland, which he said he was making. Douglas Alexander said the offer is a genuine one and that the Scotland Office is ready to work with the Scottish Government to make it happen.
The Prime Minister offered Scotland a model of localised employment support, similar to the one in England but shaped by Holyrood, in the form of DWP devolution.

In a couple of weeks the National Economic Council will meet with the First Ministers of Scotland and Wales and the First Minister and Deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland, for the first time since the Prime Minister took office, to put the offer on the table.
The Prime Minister said Scotland, the most devolved nation in the UK, is one of the most centralised nations in Europe, and called for deeper devolution in Scotland to empower all its places.
The Scottish Government has agreed to match the UK government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west of Scotland.

Great British Railways' headquarters will be built at Becketwell in Derby, with construction expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029, accommodating up to 450 GBR staff and bringing hundreds of rail jobs and an estimated £151 million boost to Derby's economy.
Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over the next four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship, with the first starters based in Derby.
Andy Burnham said that for too long people have been put up with a railway that often lets them down, and that today is another big step forward.

Heidi Alexander said Great British Railways will bring the railway together around one mission, better services for passengers, with Derby at the heart of its future, and said she was delighted Becketwell will become GBR's new home.

Pat McFadden said the government is determined to build a strong pipeline of skilled workers, and that the foundation apprenticeship forms part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities for young people to earn or learn.
Claire Ward said the GBR announcement is fantastic news for Derby, bringing hundreds of jobs and an opportunity for young people to take their first steps into work.
Around one in six young people in Scotland are not in education, employment or training.
